decided: emit grows a first-class writer for biz_provider_calls_total: RecordProviderCall(provider, op, outcome string) is added to the emit.Emitter interface and implemented on emit.Std, routed through the same buffer, label fence and drop counter every other family uses. The label fence has three parts: outcome is a closed enum of success|failed (the provider-health view the family documents and the only values the engine reads); provider and op are rejected when empty or malformed; and the number of distinct (provider, op) pairs one emitter will mint is capped, with pairs past the cap collapsing to the fixed sentinel "other" rather than being dropped. Rejections increment biz_dropped_events_total, never silence. adapters/payment/stripe's WithProviderMetric callback then wires to this in one line, and that wiring ships as a worked example.
why: ADR-0004 declares the family, all four export adapters map it, and engine/unrealized.go:295 reads biz_provider_calls_total{outcome=failed} to append its upstream-attribution hint — but nothing in the library can increment it. The only path a user following the docs has is to hand-construct an emit.MetricPoint and call Exporter.ExportMetrics directly, which bypasses the buffer, the label fence and the drop counter. That makes the engine's attribution hint dead code for every documented user, and makes the one supported workaround a cardinality hazard: ADR-0004 states cardinality protection is enforced by the emitting code itself, 'structurally impossible rather than discouraged', and the bypass path is exactly the structural hole. A writer inside emit is the only one of the three options that leaves the declared contract intact and honest. The distinct-pair cap is what makes the guarantee real rather than aspirational: ADR-0004 justifies provider and op as 'bounded by construction ... adapter-supplied constants, never request data', which is a statement about caller discipline, and the library's stated posture is not to trust caller discipline for cardinality. emit.InFlightTracker already establishes this exact pattern in this package (WithTrackerMaxItems plus an Overflowed counter), so the fence is the house style, not a new invention.
cost_if_wrong: This is an amendment to the frozen v0.1.0 emit.Emitter interface, so it breaks every out-of-tree Emitter implementation at compile time — loudly, at build, never silently at runtime. The repo is pre-1.0 and README ties v1.0.0 to surviving two external adapters, so the population of external implementers is approximately zero today and only grows; the same amendment after v1.0.0 costs a major version. If the sentinel collapse is judged wrong later, it is a one-line change to drop-and-count instead, and no persisted data shape depends on it. The inverse error — shipping v1.0.0 with a declared, adapter-mapped, engine-read metric family that the library cannot write — freezes a documented dead path into the stable contract, which is far more expensive to walk back.
alternatives: Document the hand-rolled wiring with a worked example, no API change — rejected: the documented path would bypass the buffer, the label fence and the drop counter, which is the defect the item reports, not a fix for it; it also makes ADR-0004's 'structurally impossible' claim false in the one place it is easiest to violate

Delete the attribution hint and the biz_provider_calls_total family entirely — rejected: discards a ratified ADR-0004 family that all four export adapters already map and that gives the unrealized leg its only upstream-vs-internal signal, and it touches far more surface (four adapters, six docs, the stripe ProviderCall type's stated purpose) than adding the writer

Free-form provider/op labels validated for shape only, no distinct-pair cap — rejected: shape validation rejects garbage but not a valid high-cardinality value such as a per-request op string, leaving the cardinality bill ADR-0004 exists to prevent

Take the callback rather than the values (emit owns the stripe ProviderCall shape) — rejected: emit must not depend on an adapter's type; the value-based signature keeps the dependency arrow pointing from adapters into emit
scope: emit/emit.go (Emitter interface amendment plus doc), emit/emitter.go (RecordProviderCall on Std, the label fence and its options), emit tests. Every in-tree Emitter implementation and test fake gains the method. adapters/payment/stripe: doc-comment correction on WithProviderMetric only, no behavior change. Docs corrected in the same PR per ADR-0008: the seq-stripe-webhook step table, README, semconv, adapters guide, and any prose asserting emit has no such API. No change to the metric family name, its ADR-0004 label set, the export adapters' mappings, or engine/unrealized.go's read path.
